points.description: States that the number of steps to search a node in a BST is given by the height of the tree (i.e., proportional to/at most the height h, O(h)), using the term 'height'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer relates it to tree depth/levels or path length from root without using the term height precisely.

points.description: Makes clear that this is the worst-case count, being the longest root-to-leaf path (the number of levels traversed), not the total number of nodes n.
Correctly distinguishes that the steps depend on height rather than the number of nodes: e.g., a balanced tree gives about log n steps while a skewed tree gives up to n steps.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise term 'height of the tree' as the number of steps, plus the worst-case/longest-path idea and the distinction from the node count n. Vague answers such as 'it depends on the tree' or 'a few comparisons' earn nothing. Any wrong statement, such as saying the steps always equal n or always log n, loses the point it affects.
